question.problem:
| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $\frac{1}{6}$ | $\frac{1}{9}$ | $\frac{1}{6}$ |
| $X=2$ | $\frac{1}{18}$ | $\frac{1}{18}$ | $\frac{1}{6}$ |
| $X=3$ | $\frac{1}{9}$ | $\frac{1}{9}$ | $\frac{1}{18}$ |

Compute $P(Y=0\,|\,X=3)$ given that the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above.
question.worked_solution:
By the multiplication law for conditional probability, the required probability is given by

$$
P(Y=0\,|\,X=3)=\frac{P(X=3,Y=0)}{P(X=3)}=\frac{f(3,0)}{{f}_{X}(3)},
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the marginal distribution of $X.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals. Thus,

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(3) & =f(3,0)+f(3,1)+f(3,2) \\  & =\frac{1}{9}+\frac{1}{9}+\frac{1}{18} \\  & =\frac{2}{18}+\frac{2}{18}+\frac{1}{18} \\  & =\frac{5}{18}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given table, we have that $f(3,0)=\frac{1}{9}.$ 

Finally, substituting ${f}_{X}(3)=\frac{5}{18}$ and $f(3,0)=\frac{1}{9}$ in our formula above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y=0\,|\,X=3) & =\frac{f(3,0)}{{f}_{X}(3)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{1}{9})}{(\frac{5}{18})} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
